problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+2,\,5+{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=1.$ Do not round the answers.

$a(1)=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Position Vector
examples.problem:
The position vector $\mathbf{r},$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
\mathbf{r} = \left\langle t^{5}-t^2,\, t^2+6t-3 \right\rangle.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector and the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=0.$
examples.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{5}-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+6t-3)⟩ \\  & =⟨5{t}^{4}-2t,\,2t+6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{t}^{4}-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+6)⟩ \\  & =⟨20{t}^{3}-2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=0,$ we substitute $t=0$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(0) & =⟨20(0)^{3}-2,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|\mathbf a(0)|\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(0)| & =|⟨-2,\,2⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨4{t}^{3}-2t,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(2t)⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t.$

$a=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3}-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨12{t}^{2}-2,\,\frac{1}{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(12{t}^{2}-2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨24t,\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
